title: fix: show image edit test failures in the model dashboard
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Shows the actual edit-test failure instead of claiming editing is unsupported.
- Keeps successful generation and pricing detection usable when editing fails; preserves existing modality declarations.
- Reuses the current dashboard message UI and documents the optional imageEditError response field.
- Verified: 38 endpoint service tests, Enter typecheck, Biome, and regression cases for HTTP errors, timeouts, and invalid image responses.

gist.headline: The dashboard tells the truth
gist.blurb: When an image-edit check trips over a root, the model dashboard now shows the actual pebble instead of declaring the whole garden edit-free. Generation, pricing, and modality data keep blooming as usual.
gist.summary: The community model dashboard now returns and displays an optional imageEditError for failed image-edit tests, while preserving successful generation checks, pricing detection, and existing modality declarations.
gist.impact: Model providers and dashboard users can distinguish HTTP errors, timeouts, and invalid image responses from genuinely unsupported editing without losing otherwise valid model capability and pricing information.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden inspector using a magnifying glass to read a small, clear error note attached to a code-plant labeled IMAGE EDIT, while neighboring generation and pricing plants remain healthy and flowering. A friendly CRT monitor robot can show a readable diagnostic panel, making the distinction between one failed edit check and an otherwise working model immediately visible.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel art model garden where Polli, the cute yellow-and-brown striped bee mascot with pink cheek blush, light blue wings, and tiny inspector glasses, holds a magnifying glass over a code-plant sign reading "IMAGE EDIT ERROR" while healthy flowering plants labeled "GENERATE" and "PRICING" glow beside it; a cheerful chunky CRT monitor robot displays a small clear diagnostic message. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, dark purple (#110518) outlines, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, subtle CRT glow, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, nostalgic but beautiful and emotionally warm.
